workload: One 204KB startup About page (script, style, 1800 paragraphs) checked against all 10 accelerator programs.
notes: accelerators() calls _lines once per program. _lines strips scripts, splits every block, and unescapes the page, so the same sentences are built ten times. Reusing one sentence list is the same matches; on this page that cut the call from about 178ms to about 42ms.

workload: One 221KB homepage with Shopify and WordPress fingerprints, 60 script blocks, and 900 sections.
notes: detect_tech runs each fingerprint as its own case-insensitive regex over the full homepage. The profile fingerprints are literals aside from escaped dots, so one lowercased substring scan returns the same tool list; on this page that was about 7.5x (24ms to 3.2ms).

workload: 500 discovered domains checked against one suppression list of 180 normalised domains plus a few pasted URLs and one address.
notes: Discovery calls this once per business and every call re-normalises the whole list (NFKC, regex, IDNA). The list is unchanged during a run. Normalising once into a label-boundary set keeps the same hits, subdomains, and lookalikes; on this batch that dropped about 232ms to 0.18ms.

workload: Peak traced bytes while reading addresses on a 717KB homepage with an inline script, a mailto, a data-attribute pair, and [at]/[dot] text.
notes: emails_on_page strips scripts, unescapes, and strips tags into full-page strings before scanning. tracemalloc peak is 1280109 bytes on this page; the mailto scan alone is about 2KB, so the peak is those copies. A single pass can return the same addresses without holding them.
